mechanism_narrative: A persistent increase in the federal funds rate above 2.5% over two consecutive months signals a tightening monetary regime, raising discount rates and reducing present value of future corporate cash flows, which leads to negative S&P 500 20-day forward returns.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 60% of instances when this trigger is met, or the trigger fires but the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A year-over-year decline in real personal consumption expenditures (proxied by GDPC1) of more than 2% signals weakening aggregate demand, which reduces corporate earnings expectations and drives negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained monthly decline in the unemployment rate below 3.5% for three consecutive months indicates a tight labor market, which increases wage pressures and input costs, ultimately compressing profit margins and leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not statistically different from zero at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous rise in both the federal funds rate and core CPI inflation (CPIAUCSL) above their respective 5-year averages signals a dual monetary and inflationary shock, which increases real discount rates and erodes real equity valuations, producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A coordinated monthly decline in both real personal consumption expenditures (GDPC1) and housing starts (HOUST) of more than 1% signals a broad-based weakening in demand, which reduces corporate revenue and profit expectations, leading to negative S&P 500 returns over the next 20 trading days.
candidate_trigger: GDPC1 MoM change < -1% AND HOUST MoM change < -1%
failure_condition: S&P 500 20-day forward returns are positive in more than 50% of triggered episodes, or the median return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: A persistent rise in payroll employment (PAYEMS) above its 12-month moving average, combined with a simultaneous decline in the unemployment rate (UNRATE), signals a tightening labor market that boosts wage growth and input costs, ultimately reducing profit margins and producing negative S&P 500 returns over the next 60 days in late-cycle regimes.
failure_condition: S&P 500 60-day forward returns are positive in more than 45% of triggered late-cycle episodes, or the median return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.

mechanism_narrative: An always-on negative relationship exists between the real retail sales series (RSAFS) and S&P 500 5-day forward returns: lower-than-expected monthly real retail sales growth is associated with negative short-term equity returns as it signals weakening consumer demand and near-term earnings risk.
failure_condition: S&P 500 5-day forward returns are positive in more than 55% of instances where RSAFS monthly growth is below consensus, or the median return is not significantly negative at 5% significance.
